I1.quote: A Micromeritics ASAP 2020 HD analyzer was used for surface area using nitrogen gas and low pressure hydrogen measurements.
I1.location: main, p. 451, Section 2.4 Characterization; H2 uptake isotherms in Fig. 7, p. 454

I2.quote: Searched for a measured H2 uptake on any sorbent whose majority component by mass is carbon (rGO, GO or graphite alone, or a carbon-majority composite) and found none. Fig. 7 shows H2 isotherms only for Zr-MOF and the rGO/Zr-MOF composite, and the composite contains a "relatively low quantity of rGO (1%)" (main, p. 453, Section 3); the rest is Zr-MOF, which is not a carbon sorbent under protocol 3.

I3.quote: The sorption measurements were obtained using ultra-high purity grade (99.999%) gases at 77 K. ... hydrogen measurements were conducted at only 1 bar
I3.location: main, p. 451, Section 2.4 (77 K); main, p. 454, Section 3 (1 bar); Fig. 7 x-axis, absolute pressure 0 to about 1000 mbar

I4.quote: The rGO/Zr-MOF composite had a surface area of 1480 m2/g, whereas that of pristine Zr-MOF was 1116 m2/g.
I4.location: main, p. 453, Section 3 (N2 sorption isotherms, Fig. 6, p. 454)

I5.quote: A composite material consisting of Zr-based metal organic framework (Zr-MOF) and reduced graphene oxide (rGO) was successfully synthesized by an in situ method.

notes: Decided on I2. The only H2 uptake measurements are on pristine Zr-MOF and on the rGO/Zr-MOF composite (Fig. 7). H2 uptake of rGO, GO or graphite alone is not measured. The composite is made from 0.04 g rGO added to 2.34 g ZrCl4 and 1.66 g terephthalic acid in DMF (Section 2.3), and the text gives the rGO share as 1% (p. 453). The majority component by mass is therefore the Zr-MOF, which protocol 3 excludes, so the 'carbon composites are included' clause does not apply (carbon is not the majority). The 1% is not stated explicitly as a mass basis, but the precursor masses show rGO is a small minority. A different reading of the title word 'rGO/Zr-MOF composite' as a carbon composite would flip I2 and make the paper eligible, since I1, I3, I4 and I5 are met. I1: the paper does not use the word volumetric; the instrument named is a Micromeritics ASAP 2020 HD, a static volumetric gas-sorption analyzer, and the y-axis of Fig. 7 is H2 uptake (wt.%) against absolute pressure, so I took the uptake as a measured volumetric value. Basis (excess or absolute) is not stated; not needed for eligibility. I4: the surface-area method is not named as BET in the text (N2 at 77 K on the ASAP 2020, Fig. 6), which does not matter for I4. not_primary: the paper is original experimental work. retracted: record.json is_retracted is false and the PDF shows no retraction notice. duplicate_data: not applicable; the 'as earlier reported [13]' remark on p. 453 concerns Zr-MOF crystal morphology, and the paper does not state that its H2 uptake values were published before.
